Where it began

Tom Latham was born on 2 April 1992 into a cricketing family: his father, Rod Latham, had played for New Zealand too. Tom came up through the Canterbury youth sides, captaining the under-19 team, and spent 2010 in England at the Durham academy, playing club cricket for Gateshead Fell in the North East.

His first-class career began with Canterbury in the Plunket Shield season of 2010–11, and he marked it with 65 in his first innings.

The player

His Test debut came against India in February 2014, and by July of that year he had made the opening spot his own. His first Test hundred, 103, followed in Abu Dhabi against Pakistan that November. By November 2026 he had played 95 Tests, scoring 6,450 runs at 39.09 with 17 hundreds and 31 fifties, and holding 104 catches in the field.

His best day came at the Basin Reserve in December 2018, when he carried his bat through the innings against Sri Lanka for 264 not out. Nobody had ever carried his bat to a bigger Test score. He helped New Zealand to the World Test Championship title of 2019–2021, and after being named Test captain in October 2024 he led New Zealand to a 3–0 series win in India. By November 2026 he had led them in 22 Tests and won 13.

What made him special

Latham was a careful, patient opener, and good enough against spin that New Zealand once moved him down the one-day order to deal with it. He could keep wicket as well, and when he was not wearing the gloves he usually stood close to the bat or in the slips. He collected some neat firsts along the way: the first man to make a fifty in a day-night Test, and, at Dharamshala in 2016, the first from his country to bat right through a one-day international innings.

By June 2026 only four New Zealanders had made more Test runs, and no New Zealand opener had made as many.

Away from the middle

He enjoyed his summers in English county cricket, turning out for Kent, Durham, Surrey and Warwickshire between 2016 and 2025. At Kent he made fifties in both innings of his first Championship match, something no Kent batsman had done on debut before, and at Warwickshire he marked his first game with a hundred against Surrey at Edgbaston. He also played in two World Cup finals, in 2015 and 2019.

And finally

His bowling is a short story. In top-level cricket he took a single wicket, a catch behind the stumps in a tour match after the batsman had made 209. Not long afterwards the game was abandoned, so he never found out whether he could have run through the rest.
